Level after the EQ (-24 to +24 dB).
Auto Gain: offsets the average level change of the bell and shelf bands, so a brighter or fuller setting is not judged as better just for being louder.
Zero Latency runs the bands as minimum-phase filters; Linear Phase gives the same magnitude with no phase shift (5120 samples of latency, reported for delay compensation).
uses: Everyday corrective and tonal EQ on any track, with up to eight bands
Steep low and high cuts (up to 96 dB/oct) to clean up rumble and hiss
Mid/side EQ on the mix bus: mono the lows, open up the side highs
Linear-phase mastering EQ that keeps transients and stereo image intact
Fix a single side of a stereo recording with Left or Right bands
studio_eq.properties: Eight bands in series, each a bell, shelf (RBJ), notch, band pass, or a low or high cut built as a Butterworth cascade of 1 to 16 poles (6 to 96 dB/oct; Q 0.71 is flat, higher Q lifts the corner). Each band runs on stereo, mid, side, left or right. Zero Latency: biquad cascades, no latency. Linear Phase: the same magnitude response as a 2x2 matrix per frequency bin (so mid/side and left/right bands combine exactly), turned into four 8192-tap FIRs (Hann window) and run by 16384-point FFT convolution in 1024-sample blocks; latency 5120 samples, reported for delay compensation. Auto Gain: minus the mean level change of the bell and shelf bands over 64 log-spaced points from 20 Hz to 20 kHz (mid and stereo bands count fully, left and right half, side not), within ±24 dB. The GFX and VST3/CLAP interfaces draw the response over a live spectrum (post, pre or off); drag a node to set its frequency and gain.

spectral_ducker.card_desc: Make Room for a Vocal, Band by Band
spectral_ducker.keywords: spectral ducker sidechain ducking trackspacer vocal space carve mix masking frequency ducking dynamic eq kick bass voice over 32 band
slider_desc: How deep the track can be cut in each band (0 to 100% = up to 24 dB).
Key level per band above which the track ducks (-60 to 0 dB); the dashed line in the display.
How fast the cut follows the key (0.1 to 100 ms).
How fast the track comes back when the key stops (10 to 1000 ms).
Bands below this frequency never duck (20 Hz to 5 kHz).
Bands above this frequency never duck (200 Hz to 20 kHz).
What ducks: both channels (Stereo), only the Mid, or only the Side, which keeps the centre intact and makes room at the edges.
Blend of ducked and dry track (0 to 100%).
Level after the ducker (-12 to +12 dB).
Output plays the ducked track; Delta plays only what is taken out, to hear exactly where the ducker works.
uses: Carve space for a lead vocal in a busy instrumental or pad bus
Let the kick through the bass only where they overlap
Voice-over over music that stays full between the words
Duck a reverb or delay return by the dry signal it comes from
Side-only ducking to clear the edges for a centred vocal
spectral_ducker.properties: The key (track channels 3/4, summed to mono) runs through 32 fourth-order band passes, a third of an octave apart from 30 Hz to 18 kHz; each band's level follows with Attack and Release. Every 16 samples, where a band is above Threshold, its excess (up to Amount × 24 dB) sets the cut of a Q 3 bell on the same band of the track; the bells overlap, so each cuts 0.43 of its band's amount and together they cut about the amount. Bells at 0 dB pass the signal unchanged. Stereo, mid or side; Mix and Output; Listen Delta plays dry minus ducked. Zero latency. In the Rack, the key is the Rack's dry input.

reference.card_desc: A/B Your Mix Against a Reference
reference.keywords: reference track a/b compare comparison level match loudness matched lufs short-term mix mastering correlation spectrum mono check side
slider_desc: What you hear: the Track (your mix, channels 1/2) or the Reference (channels 3/4); the switch crossfades over 10 ms.
Level Match: plays the reference at your mix's short-term loudness, so the comparison is about tone and balance, not volume.
Extra gain on the reference (-12 to +12 dB), on top of the match.
Monitor: Stereo, Mono (both channels summed) or Side (the difference only), for both sources.
uses: A/B a mix against a commercial track at the same loudness
Check a master's tonal balance and width against a reference
Compare two versions of a mix routed to the same track
Mono and side checks of mix and reference with one switch
reference.properties: Both inputs are K-weighted (ITU-R BS.1770) and measured as short-term loudness (the last 3 s, every 100 ms). With Level Match on, the reference's gain moves a tenth of the way to the difference every 100 ms (about a second to settle), within ±24 dB, and holds while either source is below -60 LUFS; Trim is added. Listen crossfades linearly over 10 ms. Monitor folds after the switch. The interfaces show both loudnesses, the reference's gain, each source's stereo correlation (averaged over about 3 s) and both spectra (each bin averaged over about a second, the reference at its played gain). No latency, no Rack module (it needs a second stereo input).

tuner.keywords: tuner chromatic strobe needle pitch guitar bass vocals strings intonation a4 415 432 440 442 baroque orchestra stage mute
slider_desc: The pitch of A4 the notes are named from, 415 to 466 Hz (440 standard, 415 baroque, 442 many orchestras).
Needle: a bar from -50 to +50 cents. Strobe: three bands that stand still in tune and move right when sharp, left when flat, faster the further off.
What is tuned: both channels summed, or only the left or right input.
Thru passes the audio; Mute silences it, for tuning on stage.
uses: Tuning guitars, basses and synths in the session
Checking a singer's or a string player's intonation
Baroque (A415) and orchestral (A442) tuning
Silent tuning on stage with Mute
tuner.properties: YIN pitch detection: the input low passed and taken down to 22 to 24 kHz, analysed about 47 times a second over the last 1024 + up to 960 samples (FFT autocorrelation, cumulative mean normalised difference, first dip below 0.15), refined by parabolas on the difference function at 1, 2, 4, 8 ... periods; within 0.25 cent from 27 Hz to 4.2 kHz on test tones. 25 Hz to about 4.5 kHz; below -70 dBFS RMS counts as silence, and the last note holds for half a second. Readings within 50 cents glide. No latency, no Rack module.

vu_meter.keywords: vu meter ppm ebu k-system k-14 k-20 level meter needle analog ballistics gain staging -18 dbfs peak hold over mastering mixing
slider_desc: VU (300 ms ballistics, average reading), PPM (EBU Type IIa peak programme meter), K-14 or K-20 (Katz RMS with the 0 mark at -14 or -20 dBFS).
The level that reads 0 in VU and PPM: a sine peaking at -24 to -8 dBFS (-18 is the EBU alignment level, -20 SMPTE).
How the held maximum (the silver mark) behaves: Off, held for 3 s, or held until you click the meters.
Monitor: Stereo, Mono (both channels summed) or Side (the difference only), after the meters.
uses: Gain staging into analog-modelled plugins at -18 dBFS
Mixing to a VU like on a console
Broadcast peak levels with an EBU PPM
Mastering with the K-14 or K-20 system
vu_meter.properties: Per channel. VU: the rectified signal through a second-order low pass (damping 0.8: about 1.5 % overshoot, 99 % in 300 ms), sine-calibrated, on the classic -20 to +3 VU dial. PPM: a peak follower charging with a 5 ms time constant (about -4 dB on a 10 ms burst) and falling 24 dB in 2.8 s, -24 to +12 around the reference. K-14 / K-20: RMS over 300 ms, sine-calibrated. OVER lights for 1 s at 0 dBFS. The audio passes through (Monitor folds it after the meters). No latency, no Rack module.

crossfeed.keywords: crossfeed headphones bs2b bauer chu moy jan meier speakers room simulation head shadow itd binaural mixing on headphones fatigue
slider_desc: Crossfeed: Bauer's headphone filter (bs2b). Speakers: two speakers in front of you, with head shadow, the time between the ears and a room.
Crossfeed: where the other side's signal starts to roll off (300 to 2000 Hz; 700 is the bs2b default, 650 Jan Meier).
Crossfeed: how far below the own side the other side arrives in the lows (1 to 15 dB; 4.5 bs2b default, 6 Chu Moy, 9.5 Jan Meier).
Speakers: how far each speaker is off centre (10 to 60 degrees; 30 is the usual stereo triangle).
Speakers: early reflections of a room (0 = none).
Blend of the dry and processed signal.
Output level (-12 to +12 dB).
uses: Mixing on headphones with less in-the-head fatigue
Checking the stereo image as it would sound on speakers
Long listening sessions on headphones
Hearing hard-panned parts as a speaker listener would
crossfeed.properties: Crossfeed: libbs2b's filter: the other side through a first-order low pass at Cutoff, Feed dB down in the lows; the own side through a matching high boost; a mono signal keeps its level in the lows and loses up to 2 dB in the highs. Speakers: Brown-Duda head-shadow filters for the near and the far ear (their high-frequency gains scaled so a mono signal keeps its level on average), Woodworth's interaural time on the far ear (0.26 ms at 30 degrees), each ear half of each; Room adds six early reflections per ear (4 to 22 ms, low passed at 5 kHz). Then Mix and Output. No latency.

de_clip.keywords: de-clip declip declipper clipping repair restoration overload distortion recorder interview dialogue peaks reconstruct audio repair
slider_desc: The level at and above which samples count as clipped (-24 to 0 dB); set it just under where the waveform flattens.
How many samples in a row must sit at the clip level before they are rebuilt (2 to 8); higher leaves natural peaks alone.
Output level (-24 to +12 dB): the rebuilt peaks pass the clip level and often 0 dBFS, so turn down here or limit after.
Listen: Output plays the result; Delta plays only what was added back.
uses: Rescuing clipped interview and dialogue recordings
Repairing a hard-clipped master or stem
Field recorder overloads
Restoring peaks before further processing
de_clip.properties: Per channel. A run of at least Min Length samples in a row at or above Clip Level is redrawn with the cubic through the two good samples on either side of it, kept on the side of the clip level it was on and at most 12 dB above it. Runs up to 120 samples are rebuilt; longer ones stay as they are. 128 samples of latency, reported for delay compensation.
